title: German Wine Classification: QbA & Prädikat
description: Understand Germany's distinctive wine classification system in depth
objectives.0: Distinguish between Tafelwein, QbA and QmP
objectives.1: Master the six-tier Prädikat sweetness system
objectives.2: Understand the link between classification and harvest ripeness
slides.0.title: German Wine Classification
slides.1.title: 🏛️ Overview of the German Classification
slides.1.content: German wine is classified by the sugar content (Oechsle reading) of the grapes at harvest, rather than by site or estate reputation. This stands in contrast to systems in Bordeaux or Burgundy, creating a philosophy built around the natural ripeness of the grape itself.
slides.2.title: 📈 The Classification from Lowest to Highest
slides.2.events.0.title: Table wine
slides.2.events.0.desc: Most basic tier, for everyday drinking
slides.2.events.1.title: Regional wine
slides.2.events.1.desc: Geographic indication; quality slightly above table wine
slides.2.events.2.title: Quality wine of designated regions
slides.2.events.2.desc: Produced in the 13 Anbaugebiete; chaptalisation permitted
slides.2.events.3.title: QmP Tier 1
slides.2.events.3.desc: Harvested at normal ripeness — light and elegant
slides.2.events.4.title: QmP Tier 2
slides.2.events.4.desc: Late harvest — rich and lusciously sweet
slides.2.events.5.title: QmP Tier 3
slides.2.events.5.desc: Selected bunches — can be sweet or dry; rich and complex
slides.2.events.6.title: QmP Tier 4
slides.2.events.6.desc: Berry-by-berry selection; influenced by noble rot; intensely sweet
slides.2.events.7.title: QmP Tier 6
slides.2.events.7.desc: TBA: dried, berry-by-berry selection — the pinnacle of sweet wine
slides.2.events.8.title: QmP Special
slides.2.events.8.desc: Frozen-grape harvest — concentrated sweetness and acidity, extremely rare
slides.3.content: In German wine, Trocken (dry) and Halbtrocken (off-dry) describe the residual sugar in the finished wine and have no direct link to Prädikat level. For example, a Spätlese Trocken is made from late-harvested grapes but fully fermented to dryness — preserving rich fruit flavours without residual sweetness.
slides.4.title: Quick Quiz
slides.4.questions.0.question: Which Prädikat level has the highest sweetness?
slides.4.questions.0.explanation: TBA (Trockenbeerenauslese) is the highest Prädikat tier, made from individually selected, shrivelled berries — yielding extreme sweetness and very small quantities.
slides.4.questions.1.question: What is the main difference between QbA and QmP?
slides.4.questions.1.options.1: QbA permits chaptalisation; QmP does not
slides.4.questions.1.options.2: QmP can only be produced in Mosel
slides.4.questions.1.explanation: QbA (Qualitätswein bestimmter Anbaugebiete) allows the addition of sugar (chaptalisation) to raise alcohol; QmP (Prädikatswein) strictly forbids it — the grapes must reach natural ripeness.
